sources.entry: cd to... - Finder Toolbar app to open the current directory in the Terminal

summary.one_liner: A small Objective-C Finder toolbar app that opens the current Finder directory in Terminal with one click.
summary.what_it_does: The app is a Finder toolbar button named "cd to....app" that opens a new Terminal window at the folder currently shown in Finder. It is written in Objective-C and uses the scripting bridge to talk to Terminal. The README says it works the same with bash, fish, and zsh. Per the changelog, selecting a package cds to its parent directory, and selecting a folder inside a package cds to that folder. Optional settings, set with `defaults write`, can close the window Terminal opens automatically on launch and choose a Terminal window theme for the windows the app opens. The README lists Universal Binary builds for Apple Silicon and Intel.
use_cases: open Terminal in the current Finder folder
jump to a folder in the terminal from Finder
add a terminal shortcut to the Finder toolbar
open a shell at the selected folder on macOS
avoid typing cd paths by hand
how_to_run: Download the latest cdto.zip from the project's releases
Copy "cd to....app" into your Applications folder
In Finder, hold ⌘ and drag the app into the Finder toolbar (or drag it from another Finder window onto the toolbar while customizing)
Click the new toolbar button to open a Terminal window at the current directory
Optional: run `defaults write name.tuley.jay.cd-to cdto-close-default-window -bool true` to close automatically opened Terminal windows
Optional: run `defaults write name.tuley.jay.cd-to cdto-new-window-setting -string "Red Sands"` to set a Terminal theme for new windows
notable: Shell agnostic: works with bash, fish, zsh, and tcsh according to the README
Uses the Scripting Bridge and Apple events, so it is fast to launch
Universal Binary for Apple Silicon and Intel (version 3.1.3)
Optional setting to close extra Terminal windows opened automatically and to apply a chosen Terminal theme
caveats: Works only with Terminal.app, since version 3.0 dropped plugins for other terminals such as iTerm
Requires macOS; the README mentions Mojave and hopefully Catalina, with no newer macOS versions named
Some features need manual `defaults write` commands
